title: Decision: which numbers 'MUST be I-JSON' allows in a log entry
description:
draft-atwood-mls-didwebvh-credential-00 §did:webvh Profile, Encoding: "Each log entry, and witness_file, MUST be I-JSON [RFC7493]". RFC 7493 §2.2 numbers are a SHOULD NOT ("SHOULD NOT include numbers that express greater magnitude or precision than an IEEE 754 double").

Readings: (a) only I-JSON's MUSTs (UTF-8, no surrogates or noncharacters, unique member names) bind; (b) "MUST be I-JSON" turns the §2.2 SHOULD NOT into a MUST NOT; (c) refuse all non-integer numbers.

Why it matters: JCS (RFC 8785) hashes numbers as doubles. A member whose JSON parser keeps 9007199254740993 exactly computes a different entryHash from one that rounds it, so members can disagree about validity.

Chosen: (b) as far as it can be checked without the number's text: a number whose value is integral and whose magnitude is above 2^53-1 is refused however written (9007199254740993, 1e20); non-integral numbers are accepted as serde_json parses them, so excess precision (3.141592653589793238) is not detected. Noncharacters are refused in strings and member names; duplicate names are compared after unescaping. JSON nesting deeper than serde_json's 128 levels is refused (the draft sets no limit). crates/mls-didwebvh/src/json.rs. For -01: say which numbers are allowed (simplest: integers within ±(2^53-1) only; did:webvh needs no others) and give a nesting limit.
close_reason: Chosen by agent per the reading in the description; recorded in docs/didwebvh-draft-feedback.md for -01; flag to Mark
